decisions.reason: The candidate's existing message-143 MODIFY already defines the commission recipient dynamically as the holder of the NFT whose referral code was used, which includes a purchaser who becomes the current holder after transfer.
The existing message-143 MODIFY already assigns the referral commission allocation to the holder of the NFT whose code was used, so the post-transfer recipient semantics are fully represented.
The FAQ requirement already directs publication of the complete message-143 Q&A, and the source decision does not require a separate change to that copy requirement.
Changing who receives a referral commission after NFT transfer does not change Big Block prize amounts, ticket rules, funding, or draw behavior.
The source Event changes commission-recipient semantics, not the referral code's source, permanence, or display locations; NFT transfer semantics are maintained by the source Requirement.
Changing the post-transfer commission recipient does not alter Small Block prize amounts, ticket eligibility, reset rules, funding, or draw conditions.
The source decision concerns referral commissions on future mints and does not change secondary-sale royalty amounts, allocations, enforcement, or ticket-generation rules.
The commission-recipient change does not alter badge thresholds, award destination, enabled badges, or current badge function.
The candidate already states that a wallet is required to receive affiliate commission payments; identifying the current NFT holder as recipient does not change fiat access or wallet requirements.
Referral commission ownership after NFT transfer does not affect prize announcement channels, claim method, or claim-page location.
The source decision does not change the Transak provider, supported payment methods, conversion behavior, or preexisting crypto and wallet requirements for minting.
Changing the recipient of a referral commission after transfer does not change the $15 primary mint price or its no-hidden-fees condition.
